narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Quiet Research Desk"**

A calm, precise research dashboard in the category standard, executed at the craft bar of Linear and Stripe Dashboard. White panels sit on a cool grey canvas, hairline borders and soft shadows separate the layers, and one blue carries everything the reader can act on. The first screen ranks the best opportunities, and every number opens onto its reasoning. Alignment, tabular figures and restraint do the work; nothing on the page shouts.

Density is high but legible. One ranked list replaces tabs, and depth lives behind disclosure rather than being cut: a row expands into its cases, valuation, analyst evidence and sources. The page is desktop-first with a sticky "This week" rail; on a phone the table becomes a stacked list and the top cards become a sideways scroller. Light and dark themes are both first-class, following the system setting unless the reader picks one in the top bar.

The world rejects two things by name: the trading-app look (neon, hype, casino darkness, loud green and red fills) and the spreadsheet dump.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey canvas, white panels, 1px hairlines, 12px corners, soft two-layer shadows.
Inter alone, semibold headings with tight negative tracking, tabular figures everywhere a number appears.
One blue accent for action, selection, sort and the current place; green and red only for gain and loss.
Our view leads: the close, our 12-month target and the upside carry the weight; the Wall St. average is a muted, separately labelled reference, never blended.
Every range bar shares one scale, so rows compare at a glance.
Keyboard-first list with visible kbd hints.

rules.name: The Two Bases Rule
rules.body: Our estimate and the Wall St. average are never blended into one number. Each has its own labelled column and its own sort, and `#` always shows our rank, even when the list is sorted by something else (a sort note says so).

rules.name: The Our-View-Leads Rule
rules.body: The page is about three numbers: the close, our 12-month target and the upside between them. Wall St. is a reference: muted grey, the last column, absent from the cards, its weekly moves listed last.

rules.name: The Dated Close Rule
rules.body: Prices are named by when they were set ("Close · Nov 20", "Prices at the Nov 20, 2026 close"). Never "now", "today" or "current".

rules.name: The Meaningful Colour Rule
rules.body: Green and red mean gain and loss, and their direct analogues (Buy and Sell, upgrade and downgrade, a target strip's high and low). Amber means caution. Blue means you can act here, or this is selected, sorted or current. No hue is ever decorative.

rules.name: The Wash Not Fill Rule
rules.body: State colour appears as text, or as text on its own 13%-strength wash. There are no solid green or red blocks.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can sit above another number uses tabular figures, so columns align without monospace.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, headers and labels are sentence case at their natural size. No uppercase tracking, no eyebrow labels above headings.

rules.name: The Desktop First Rule
rules.body: The desktop layout is the reference. Phones get a purpose-built stacked list and a sideways card scroller, not a squeezed table.

rules.name: The Lift Means Open Rule
rules.body: Only elements that open something rise on hover. Static panels never move.

rules.name: The Shared Scale Rule
rules.body: Every range bar on the page uses one scale, computed from the whole ranked list, with a dashed zero tick. A hollow ghost ring marks last week's base case whenever it moved by half a point or more.

dos: **Do** keep our estimate and the Wall St. average in separate, labelled columns with separate sorts, and keep `#` as our rank.
**Do** put our base-case price target ahead of market cap wherever both appear; market cap is supporting detail.
**Do** draw every range bar on the one shared scale, with the ghost ring for last week's base case.
**Do** use tabular figures for every number and Inter for every word.
**Do** keep panels at 12px corners, inner cards at 10px, controls at 8px and pills at 999px, with 1px hairlines and the rest shadow.
**Do** show the disclaimer ("Research output, not investment advice") in both the lede and the footer.
**Do** put depth behind disclosure (row detail, "Show N more", "Weighting checks") instead of removing it.
donts: **Don't** use green or red for anything but gain and loss and their direct analogues, and never as a solid fill.
**Don't** use blue for decoration; it marks action, selection, sort and the current place.
**Don't** blend our estimate and the Street into one number or one sort.
**Don't** add neon colour, glowing effects or a dark casino mood; dark mode is a near-black canvas with raised panels and the same restraint.
**Don't** add a second typeface, uppercase eyebrow labels or kicker text above headings.
**Don't** squeeze the desktop table onto a phone; use the stacked list.
